item.title: How is coffee culture evolving? 咖啡文化正在发生怎样的变化？
item.description:
“Coffee（咖啡）”——这种发源于非洲的苦涩饮品，如今已经成为许多人的最爱。在世界许多地区，咖啡早已形成独特的传统和文化，并发展出数不胜数的品种和享用方式。随着一代代咖啡消费者观念和习惯的变化，人们享用咖啡的方式发生了哪些改变？又有哪些新元素在引领咖啡文化的潮流？阅读本文，了解这一古老饮品的当代 “进化史”。

词汇：coffee culture 咖啡文化

1  Coffee is one of the most popular drinks in the world. In Italy, espresso is often enjoyed quickly like a shot, whereas Scandinavian coffee culture places more emphasis on taking time to enjoy coffee socially. In Ethiopia, which is often considered the birthplace of coffee, they take their coffee culture very seriously, and drinking coffee can last several hours. Freshly roasted beans are ground by hand, then brewed in a special clay pot before being served in small cups and enjoyed in three rounds, each round symbolising deeper community connection and blessing. The way people drink coffee is rooted in tradition, but it's also changing. According to a BBC News article with the headline Coffee Price Surges to Highest on Record, coffee is the world's second most traded commodity by volume, and its popularity is increasing, perhaps because of new drinking cultures.  

2  Drinking coffee doesn't just give you a boost of energy. It's been known to have some health benefits too. According to BMJ, a peer-reviewed medical journal, an analysis of nearly 220 studies found that coffee drinkers may enjoy more overall health benefits, such as a lower risk of specific cancers and neurological, metabolic, and liver conditions.Some young adults are also becoming more interested in coffee with additional health benefits. Hardtank's research into Gen Z coffee trends suggests that young consumers are becoming more interested in health-conscious coffee, for those who actively care about physical, mental, and nutritional well-being. Drink Ripples also reports that 38% of consumers will pay more for drinks with added health benefits. Blends that use mushroom powder, proteins and collagen are also gaining popularity.

3  The drink also has to look the part. Pure Gusto's research into UK cafe trends highlights how customers want drinks that are more exciting. There has been a surge in using unusual ingredients with interesting flavours and creating colourful and fun aesthetics for drinks. Ingredients such as ube and black sesame are appearing in specialty drinks, while sweet and savoury combinations such as miso caramel are making traditional coffee more adventurous. These ingredients, along with toppings such as cold foam and cream, are becoming more popular.

4  So, how do you take your coffee? Are you more traditional in your method of preparing coffee with boiled water and perhaps a splash of milk or a bit of sugar? Or do you love mixing in syrups to create sweeter flavours and pouring your concoction into a clear cup and adding toppings to show off your coffee creativity?

测验与练习

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 _______
Paragraph 2 _______
Paragraph 3 _______
Paragraph 4 _______

a. Coffee traditions around the world
b. Health-conscious coffee
c. How do you take yours?
d. The hidden cost of coffee
e. More than just a drink

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. 1. Which country's people drink a small amount of coffee very quickly?
a. Ethiopia
b. Finland
c. Italy

2. Coffee is the world's most traded commodity by volume.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

3. According to Drink Ripples, more than half of consumers are willing to pay more for coffee with added health benefits.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

4. What does "These ingredients" refer to in the following sentence? These ingredients, along with toppings such as cold foam and cream…
a. coffee beans from Ethiopia
b. toppings, such as cold foam and cream
c. unusual ingredients such as ube, black sesame and miso caramel

5. People add syrup to their coffee to make it…
a. bitter.
b. cold.
c. sweet.

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Coffee culture is changing as the modern 1) _______ becomes more interested in healthier and more exciting drinks. The popularity of specialty 2) _______ and using ingredients for an 3) _______ have increased. This could reflect that people are perhaps more 4) _______ these days, or that their most important motive for purchasing a coffee is so that it 5) _______.

aesthetic
blends
boosts
consumer
health-conscious
looks the part
peer-reviewed

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

shot 一小杯（浓缩咖啡等）
birthplace 发源地
roasted 烘焙过的
grind 把…磨成粉，磨碎
brew 冲泡，煮制
blessing 祝福
rooted 源自，植根于
commodity 大宗商品
boost 提振，提升
peer-reviewed 经同行评审的
consumer 消费者
health-conscious 注重健康的
nutritional 营养的
blend （咖啡豆的）拼配，混合配方
look the part 外观符合自身定位，看起来够格
surge 激增，急剧上升
aesthetics 美学，审美
savoury 咸味的
topping （浇在食物顶部的）配料
foam 泡沫
splash 少量（液体）；一点点
syrup 糖浆
concoction 调制品，混合物
show off 展示，炫耀

答案

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 a) Coffee traditions around the world
Paragraph 2 b) Health-conscious coffee
Paragraph 3 e) More than just a drink
Paragraph 4 c) How do you take yours?

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. c. In Italy,espresso is often enjoyed quickly like a shot, …

2. False. According to a BBC article, coffee is the world's second most traded commodity by volume and its popularity is increasing, perhaps because of new drinking cultures.

3. b. False. Drink Ripples reports that 38% of consumers will pay more for drinks with added health benefits.

4. c. Ingredients such as ube and black sesame are appearing in specialty drinks, while sweet and savoury combinations such as miso caramel are making traditional coffee more adventurous. These ingredients, along with toppings such as cold foam and cream, can cost more than traditional coffee ingredients.

5. c. … or do you love mixing in syrups to create sweeter flavours and pouring your concoction into a clear cup to see all of your coffee creativity?

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Coffee culture is changing as the modern consumer becomes more interested in healthier and more exciting drinks. The popularity of specialty blends and using ingredients for an aesthetic have increased. This could reflect that people are perhaps more health-conscious these days, or that their most important motive for purchasing a coffee is so that it looks the part.

item.title: Why it is so hard to start exercising 为什么开始锻炼如此困难
item.description:
我们都知道锻炼的益处，但许多人仍缺乏足够的运动。事实上，缺乏运动本身也可能成为一种习惯，而改变习惯往往并非易事。除此之外，锻炼需要付出体力和精力，而人类在进化过程中可能逐渐形成了避免不必要能量消耗的倾向。这样看来，不难理解为什么许多人的运动量始终达不到建议水平。

词汇：exercise 锻炼

1 Exercise. We know it's great, both for our physical and mental health, and it's one of the easiest ways to feel better. The recommendation for most adults is to do 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week. However, the UN has estimated that 1.8 billion people across the world don't manage to do this. So, what's stopping us?

2 We may have evolved to avoid exercise. According to evolutionary biologist Daniel Lieberman, because early humans needed energy for hunting, we developed an instinct not to waste this energy on seemingly pointless exercises. Of course, now our lifestyles have changed dramatically, but this instinct remains to some degree, pulling us towards our sofas. We naturally like to relax. 

3 Often we have to fight against our habits. Many of us will have developed a habit of inactivity and changing this is hard. Psychologist Brad Stennerson tells us that some research shows it can take at least six weeks to make an exercise routine habitual. The good news is that once we make exercise a habit, it's a lot easier to keep going. It may be that what we need to focus on are the cues that lead us to start exercising. This could be the time of day, or the start or finish of another activity. Psychology professor Alison Phillips calls this the instigation habit, and her research suggests that is key to develop an exercise routine. If you decide that you will do exercise as soon as you finish work, this may make it easier to stick to.

4 Let's not forget that exercise feels like hard work. And in fact, it's starting it that often feels the worst. This is because your muscles suddenly demand energy and your body has to work out where to get it from. Sport scientist Richard Taylor explains that it can take 10-15 minutes for your body to find an equilibrium and provide the muscles' needs easily. One thing to remember is that exercise doesn't necessarily need to be highly intensive. The recent trend in South Korea for slow jogging, where people jog at a slow enough speed to chat comfortably, helps to remind us that big health gains can be found by moving from no activity to some activity.

5 If you're looking to start an exercise regime, most experts offer the same advice. Find something that you enjoy. Start with small goals and try to stay consistent. That makes it easier to build up a habit and before you know it, it will be part of your routine.

测验与练习

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 _______
Paragraph 2 _______
Paragraph 3 _______
Paragraph 4 _______
Paragraph 5 _______

a. Changing habits
b. Many of us inactive
c. Tips to get started
d. Evolved to relax
e. The easiest exercise to start
f.  The toughest 10 minutes

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. 1.8bn people get less than 2.5 hours' moderate exercise a week.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

2. According to evolutionary biologists, early humans used exercise to get better at hunting.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

3. It can take longer than a month to make exercise a habit.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

4. What does 'this' refer to in the following sentence? This could be time of day, or the start or finish of another activity.
a. exercise
b. cues
c. a habit

5. Our bodies are able to immediately provide all the energy needed for exercise.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Official recommendations say that we should get 150 minutes of 1) _______ exercise a week. Many people are currently 2) _______ and would benefit by starting exercise. The problem is that it can be difficult to make it 3) _______. Experts say that starting slow, and choosing an activity that you like will help you make exercise part of your 4) _______. Remember, gentle exercise like slow jogging can also provide significant 5) _______.

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

physical 身体上的
mental 心理上的
moderate 适度的，适中的
waste 浪费
relax 放松
habit 习惯
inactivity 缺乏活动，不活动
routine 日常惯例，例行安排
habitual 习惯性的
cue 诱因；触发信号
instigation habit 启动习惯
stick to 坚持
muscle 肌肉
energy 能量
equilibrium 平衡；平衡状态
intensive 高强度的
jogging 慢跑
health gains 健康益处
regime （健康、饮食等）方案
goal 目标
consistent 始终如一的，持续稳定的

答案

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 b) Many of us inactive
Paragraph 2 d) Evolved to relax
Paragraph 3 a) Changing habits
Paragraph 4 f) The toughest 10 minutes
Paragraph 5 c) Tips to get started

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. a. True. The recommendation for most adults is to do 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week. However, the UN has estimated that 1.8 billion people across the world don't manage to do this.

2. b. False. According to evolutionary biologist Daniel Lieberman, because early humans needed energy for hunting, we developed an instinct to not waste this energy on seemingly pointless exercises.

3. a. True. Psychologist Brad Stennerson tells us that some research shows it can take at least six weeks to make an exercise routine habitual.

4. b. 'This' refers to the cues mentioned in the previous sentence.

5. b. False. Sport scientist Richard Taylor explains that it can take 10-15 minutes for your body to find an equilibrium and provide the muscles' needs easily.

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Official recommendations say that we should get 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week. Many people are currently inactive and would benefit by starting exercise. The problem is that it can be difficult to make it habitual. Experts say that starting slow, and choosing an activity that you like will help you make exercise part of your routine. Remember, gentle exercise like slow jogging can also provide significant health gains.

item.title: Return of the sleeper train in Europe 欧洲卧铺列车再度兴起
item.description:
曾几何时，“sleeper train（卧铺列车）” 是人们长途出行的热门选择。乘坐卧铺列车不仅能节省一晚住宿费用，还能在睡梦中舒适地抵达目的地。但随着 “budget airline（廉价航空公司）” 的兴起，许多人开始转而选择速度更快、价格更低的航空出行。如今，随着越来越多的人倾向于选择更环保的出行方式，卧铺列车在欧洲正重新受到欢迎。除了环保因素外，卧铺列车的支持者们还指出，铁路旅行本身也拥有飞机难以替代的独特魅力和体验。

词汇：transport 交通

1  The Sun has set, and you're headed to a train station in Stockholm with your overnight bag. You board the sleeper train, change into your comfortable clothes, enjoy the scenery through the window for a while before laying your head down to rest. Snoring from the other passengers in your shared cabin delays your bedtime, but the gentle motion and white noise eventually send you to sleep. The next morning, just over 12 hours later, you wake up in Germany's second largest city, Hamburg. "It still sounds like a long time, but you go to sleep, and it's such a nice atmosphere on the train," says Julia Senninger, a fan of sleeper trains.

2  Before budget airlines made flights across Europe so quick and cheap, sleeper trains were a popular way to cover large distances without wasting daylight or paying for a place to stay. After a period of decline, sleeper trains in Europe are making a comeback. Belgian-Dutch company European Sleeper launched the Brussels to Milan route in September 2026 and has announced a new route connecting Belgium, the Netherlands and Sweden, scheduled to open in 2028. Other train companies Trenitalia and Nightjet have also announced plans for new international routes. Companies are rushing to meet high demand.

3  The rise in popularity is partly due to changing attitudes and increased awareness surrounding climate change. The carbon footprint of an electric-powered train is just a fraction of a flight. But there's more to it. Sleeper train fan Julia Senninger says trains are simply more fun. You meet more people and can have interesting conversations. Cat Jones, founder of the flight-free travel agency Byway, says, "The point of travel is the experience rather than just the arrival." So, people are buying into the idea that the journey to your destination is also part of the trip. Besides the convenience of starting and ending your journey in a city centre, there's also a sense of romance and adventure when you imagine whizzing through unknown landscapes and foreign villages while you sleep.

4  In Europe, the sleeper train comeback does not come without challenges. Competing with budget airlines, some sleeper train routes have disappeared, even while new ones have launched. Problems with infrastructure, cost and availability mean that the high demand for a more sustainable travel option is not currently being met. 

测验与练习

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 _______
Paragraph 2 _______
Paragraph 3 _______
Paragraph 4 _______

a. The sleeper train's second rise
b. A sleeper train scene
c. Sleeper trains outside Europe
d. Why people like sleeper trains
e. Not a perfect solution
f.  The downfall of budget airlines

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. What's mentioned as something that might keep you awake on a sleeper train?
a. snoring
b. white noise
c. train motion

2. European Sleeper opened a route connecting Belgium and Sweden in 2026.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

3. Sleeper trains are more environmentally friendly than airplanes.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

4. Which word best summarises Julia Senninger and Cat Jones feelings about train travel?
a. efficient
b. enjoyable
c. cheap

5. The UK is investing much more into sleeper train travel than Italy.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

There is a 1) _______ for sleeper trains in Europe due to an increased awareness of climate change. People also enjoy the 2) _______ of beginning and ending a journey in the middle of the city. One difficulty train companies have is that they are competing with 3) _______ on cost and efficiency. But fans of sleeper trains argue that it's not just about the 4) _______, it's about enjoying the 5) _______.

carbon footprint
destination
high demand
convenience
board
budget airlines
journey

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

board 登上（交通工具）
snoring 打鼾，鼾声
white noise 白噪音
budget airline 廉价航空公司，低成本航空公司
make a comeback 卷土重来，重新流行
high demand 旺盛的需求
carbon footprint 碳足迹
there is more to it 事情并没有这么简单，事实不止如此
buy into something 认同；接受；相信某个观点、想法或说法
journey 旅途，旅程
destination 目的地
trip 旅行
convenience 便利
whizz 飞驰而过，“嗖” 地掠过
infrastructure 基础设施

答案

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 b) A sleeper train scene
Paragraph 2 a) The sleeper train's second rise
Paragraph 3 d) Why people like sleeper trains
Paragraph 4 e) Not a perfect solution

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. a. Snoring from the other passengers in your shared booth delays your bedtime, but the gentle motion and white noise eventually send you to sleep.

2. b. False. Belgian-Dutch company European Sleeper launched the Brussels to Milan route in September 2026 and has announced a new route connecting Belgium, the Netherlands and Sweden, scheduled to open in 2028.

3. a. True. The carbon footprint of an electric-powered train is just a fraction of a flight.

4. b. Sleeper train fan Julia Senninger says trains are simply more fun. Cat Jones says, "The point of travel is the experience rather than just the arrival."

5. c. Not given. Train travel in the UK is not mentioned. 

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

There is a high demand for sleeper trains in Europe due to an increased awareness of climate change. People also enjoy the convenience of beginning and ending a journey in the middle of the city. One difficulty train companies have is that they are competing with budget airlines on cost and efficiency. But fans of sleeper trains argue that it's not just about the destination, it's about enjoying the journey.

item.title: Is social media still 'social'? 社交媒体还 “社交” 吗？
item.description:
社交媒体最初旨在帮助人们保持联系，但随着越来越多的人被动地使用这些平台，每天花上数小时浏览信息流，社交媒体是否正在失去其 “社交性” 呢？

词汇：social media 社交媒体

1 For many people, social media is a normal part of everyday life. It's used to keep in touch, entertain and follow what's happening in the world. But numbers from DataReportal indicate that the average use of social media is around two hours 21 minutes a day. That's nearly 15 hours per week or about 32 days a year! The same report also mentions that people are using social media more passively. This means they're spending a lot of time scrolling on their feed, sending memes and reacting to things with emojis instead of sending messages. Could it be that social media platforms are negatively impacting the way we interact with people, and are they taking time away from us actually being social?

2 One study looked at what happened when social media was deliberately limited. In The effect of self-monitoring limited social media use on psychological well-being, researchers in the United States studied 230 university students. One group was asked to limit social media use to 30 minutes a day, while the other continued without a limit. After two weeks, the group limiting its use reported lower levels of loneliness, depression, anxiety and FOMO.

3 Sleep is another part of the picture. For many people, scrolling through social media has become part of their bedtime routine when they should be winding down to rest. Research published by the National Library of Medicine has examined the effects of blue light from electronic screens. This light can affect the body's natural sleep-wake cycle and increase alertness. Reducing screen time before bed may therefore help some people prepare for sleep. Better sleep can also provide more energy for work, hobbies and lay the groundwork for more successful and fulfilling face-to-face social interactions.

4 These findings do not necessarily mean that you have to completely quit social media. Instead, it may be worth considering how much time is being spent online, and what that time could be used for instead. Small changes might include moving the social media app away from the home screen, using social media only at certain times, or accessing it through a computer rather than the phone you probably have with you all the time. The idea is not to disconnect from the online world completely, but to create a better balance between online and offline life. Reducing the use of social media could free up time to take part in more rewarding hobbies and encourage you to connect with people in real life rather than through a screen.

测验与练习

一、为本文选择总结句。

a. Limiting social media use may have benefits for wellbeing and sleep.
b. Social media is harmful to everyone and should be completely avoided.
c. Social media is mainly useful for maintaining relationships.

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. What point does the writer make by converting the daily social media figure into a weekly and yearly figure?
a. Even a small amount of daily use can add up to a substantial amount of time over a longer period.
b. Social media use has increased compared with previous years.
c. Most people spend approximately 15 hours of every week communicating with friends online.

2. What was the main difference between the two groups in the study?
a. One group monitored its psychological wellbeing, while the other monitored its social media use.
b. One group reduced its social media use to a specific daily limit, while the other was not given a limit.
c. One group stopped using social media completely, while the other continued using it for 30 minutes a day.

3. Reducing screen time before bed may help people prepare for sleep.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

4. Which of the following is NOT suggested as a way of reducing social media use?
a. Limiting social media to particular times of the day.
b. Moving social media apps away from the phone's home screen.
c. Removing social media accounts from the phone altogether.

5. Reducing the time you spend on your phone could mean that you have more time for social media.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

A study found that when university students 1) _______ limited their social media use, they reported lower levels of loneliness, anxiety and 2) _______. Researchers also found that social media use before bed can affect the 3) _______ and increase 4) _______. In addition, reducing time on social media can 5) _______ more time for hobbies and real-life social interaction.

alertness
deliberately
indicate
free up
FOMO
passively
sleep-wake cycle

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

keep in touch 保持联系
indicate 表明，显示
passively 被动地
feed （社交媒体上的）信息流，动态
meme 网络梗；梗图
emoji 表情符号
deliberately 刻意地
self-monitoring 自我监控
FOMO 错失恐惧，错失焦虑（Fear Of Missing Out 的缩写）
part of the picture 整体情况的一部分；一个方面或因素
wind down （活动之后）放松下来，让身心平静下来
sleep-wake cycle 睡眠觉醒周期
alertness 清醒程度；警觉性
lay the groundwork 为…打下基础，为…做好准备
fulfilling 令人愉快满足的，有成就感的
face-to-face 面对面的
access 访问；使用
free up 腾出，空出
rewarding 有意义的；有成就感的

答案

一、 为本文选择总结句。

a. Limiting social media use may have benefits for wellbeing and sleep.

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. a. But numbers from DataReportal indicate that the average use of social media is around two hours 21 minutes a day. That's nearly 15 hours per week or about 32 days a year!

2. b. One group was asked to limit social media use to 30 minutes a day, while the other continued without a limit.

3. a. True. This light can affect the body's natural sleep-wake cycle and increase alertness.

4. c. Small changes might include moving the social media app away from the home screen, using social media only at certain times, or accessing it through a computer rather than the phone you probably have with you all the time.

5. b. False. Reducing the use of social media could free up time to take part in more rewarding hobbies and encourage you to connect with people in real life rather than through a screen.

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

A study found that when university students deliberately limited their social media use, they reported lower levels of loneliness, anxiety and FOMO Researchers also found that social media use before bed can affect the sleep-wake cycle and increase alertness. In addition, reducing time on social media can free up more time for hobbies and real-life social interaction.

item.title: Why we like collecting things 我们为什么喜欢收藏东西
item.description:
很多人都有收藏的爱好，有人喜欢收集大自然中的物品，有人会珍藏旅途中的纪念品，也有人收藏能唤起童年回忆的东西。我们为什么如此热衷于收藏？拥有大量收藏品又会给我们带来哪些好处和困扰？

词汇：collecting 收藏

1 People collect all sorts of things. I collect fridge magnets, so my fridge has slowly become a colourful map of everywhere I've been. I also have fond memories of collecting rocks and shells from the beach with my mum when we’d visit the coast in summer. It’s true that some people collect natural objects such as fossils and interesting stones, while others bring home souvenirs from their travels. There are also people collecting miniature versions of real commercial products and tiny replicas of familiar objects, for example scaled-down retro toys, classic board games and action figures. In this way, collectables can be both decorative and functional, giving us something nostalgic to look at or fiddle with when bored.

2 But why do people have such a strong desire to collect things? One explanation is that collecting gives us a sense of order and achievement. Happiful, a mental health and wellbeing magazine, wrote that adding to a collection creates a sense of progress and accomplishment. According to an article published in the Journal of Consumer Research, titled Seeking Structure in Collections: Desire for Control Motivates Engagement in Collecting, collecting can help people feel more in control. It explains that collections can become an extension of our identity. The things we collect reflect our hobbies, interests and loyalties.

3 However, not everyone believes collecting is beneficial. Advocates of minimalism argue that owning fewer possessions improves wellbeing. As Beverley D'Silva reported for the BBC, the simplicity associated with a minimalist lifestyle may even contribute to greater happiness. From this perspective, filling our homes with collections can seem more like unnecessarily hoarding clutter. There is also an important distinction between thoughtfully curating your collection and simply accumulating more possessions. The Journal of Consumer Research article warns that some collectors can be drawn into excessive spending, especially when companies release new or rare additions to collections that were once considered complete. In those cases, collecting may be driven less by passion and more by pressure.

4 Despite this, collecting remains as popular as ever. Perhaps the reason collecting endures is simple – collections tell stories. And displaying these collections can be just as satisfying as finding them. Happiful describes collections as a kind of self-portrait, reflecting our interests, personality and memories. Whether it's fridge magnets, shells or action figures, the real value often lies not in the objects themselves, but in the memories and meanings attached to them.

item.title: The UK's favourite type of humour 英国人钟爱的幽默形式
item.description:
在英国，“laughing at oneself（自嘲）” 被许多人视为英国文化中极具代表性的一种幽默形式。当人们陷入困境时，适度的自嘲不仅可以拉近彼此之间的距离，还能缓解面对压力时的焦虑和紧张情绪。不过，对于那些难以接受自己成为玩笑对象的人来说，这种幽默风格并不容易掌握。什么情况下自嘲能展现幽默感？又在什么情况下可能适得其反，带来更多问题呢？本文将简要介绍自嘲这一独特的幽默形式。

词汇：humour 幽默

1  Over two thirds of Brits agree that being able to laugh at yourself, or what we call 'self-deprecating humour', is a defining part of British culture, according to a recent survey by the charity Comic Relief. British comedian Sir Lenny Henry says it's not about putting yourself down, it's about bringing people together. After years of doing stand-up comedy, Lenny says that laughing at yourself is "one of the quickest ways to feel connected to a room full of strangers". But when is it good, and when is it bad, to make fun of yourself? Can it be taken too far?

2  When a person points out their own flaws in a light-hearted way, it can make them seem more human and make others feel comfortable. A 2025 study called 'When Laughter Hurts and Helps' linked the joy of being laughed at with higher social connectedness, in other words, a greater sense of belonging to a group. Conversely, the trait 'gelotophobe', or someone who fears being laughed at, has been linked to greater friendship avoidance and lower life satisfaction. Even leaders might benefit from self-deprecating humour. Lecturer at Stanford Graduate School of Business Naomi Bagdonas says that for today's leaders, 'Humour is an elixir for trust and an antidote to arrogance'.

3  Making light of negative situations can also be a coping mechanism. Imagine you're working on a group project, and something goes wrong. While everyone is panicking and trying to find someone to blame, you say sarcastically, "Well, this is going well!" This gives people permission to laugh a bit, and they might feel more positively about the situation. The challenge doesn't vanish, but at least people feel less tense and could feel more able to deal with the situation. A 2024 study published in Europe's Journal of Psychology found that maintaining a humorous perspective when things go wrong can lead to greater resilience.

4  Of course, there's always a balance. While self-deprecating humour can bring people closer and make bad situations less overwhelming, it's important that it doesn't come from a place of bitterness and self-hatred. It's best to make jokes about yourself only once you've made peace with the flaw or mistake you're making fun of. 

测验与练习

一、为本文选择总结句。

b. Laughing at oneself is seen as overall negative.
c. Laughing at oneself is seen as overall neutral.

c. Not given

a. True
b. False
c. Not given

a. True
b. False
c. Not given

4. According to the article, making light of a bad situation…
a. removes the challenges.
b. makes people feel better.
c. makes people feel tense.

5. Self-deprecation is always good.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

In the UK, 1) _______ is popular. The point is to 2) _______ of yourself in a 3) _______ way. Research says this type of humour can lead to higher 4) _______, but it's important not to 5) _______. First, make sure you have made peace with your flaws to avoid making others feel awkward.

make fun

put yourself down
social connectedness
bitterness
self-deprecating humour
light-hearted

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

comedian 喜剧演员
put oneself down 贬低自己，看轻自己，否定自己

答案

3. c. Not given. Naomi Bagdonas says that for today's leaders, 'Humour is an elixir for trust and an antidote to arrogance', but such a strong claim is not made.

4. b. The challenge doesn't vanish, but at least people feel less tense and could feel more able to deal with the situation.

5. b. False. While self-deprecating humour can bring people closer and make bad situations less overwhelming, it's important that it doesn't come from a place of bitterness and self-hatred.

item.title: Daydreaming: a distraction or a vehicle for ideas? 白日梦：让人分心的干扰，还是灵感的来源？
item.description:
你觉得 “daydreaming（做白日梦）” 是一件好事吗？许多人在做白日梦时会从眼前的事情中分心，无法专注于当下。但一些研究表明，放空大脑、让思绪自由地 “漫游” 有助于思考并提升创造力。本文探讨做白日梦的益处与其带来的问题。

词汇：daydreaming 做白日梦

1  Daydreaming has a bad reputation – we say things like "he's away with the fairies" or "she has her head in the clouds" implying these people are inattentive, easily distracted, maybe even lazy. Is this reputation justified? Or is a trip to la-la land actually something that might benefit us?

2  First, it's important to differentiate daydreaming from mind wandering. Mind wandering happens when you're busy with a task and your mind disengages from it, whereas daydreaming happens when you're doing nothing and spontaneous thoughts unrelated to your surroundings pop up. In a review of research called 'The costs and benefits of mind-wandering', the authors found mind wandering negatively impacted reading comprehension, attention, memory and intelligence. None of that sounds great, so are there any benefits at all?

3  Activities that allow your mind to wander, like having a bath or meditating can lead to the 'aha' moment that you've been waiting for, which is why people often say they have their best ideas in the shower. This might work in the workplace too. In a 2021 study called 'Zoning out or breaking through? Linking daydreaming to creativity in the workplace', the authors concluded that "daydreaming carries noteworthy benefits for creativity". In other words, daydreaming at work may help you to come up with solutions to your problems.  It's also suggested that daydreaming can provide a sort of mental escape, both from the difficulty of the task, but also from the stresses of everyday life.

4  So, it seems daydreaming might be a bit of a double-edged sword, and the extent to which it provides benefits rather than downsides depends on things like how positive the thoughts are as well as your ability to identify and control them. If you find yourself endlessly staring into space, pondering the meaning of life while you're trying to get things done, why not try a mindfulness technique?

5  Observe the thoughts as they pop up, visualise them as clouds and watch them pass by. Alternatively, when you've got some time to yourself, instead of reading a book or listening to music, why not let yourself get lost in thought?

3. a. True. Linking daydreaming to creativity in the workplace', the authors concluded that "daydreaming carries noteworthy benefits for creativity".

item.title: Portable fan problems 手持小风扇引发的问题
item.description:
近年来，手持小风扇逐渐成为了炎炎夏日里的 “时尚单品”。不过，有研究指出，廉价、劣质的手持小风扇以及其它各类 “fast technology（快科技）” 产品往往容易被人们用后即弃。这不仅会增加电子垃圾的数量，还会给垃圾回收设施带来安全隐患，并可能导致重金属污染。本文简要介绍手持小风扇给人类社会和自然环境带来的问题。

词汇：electronic fans 电风扇

1  They could be the hottest accessory of an even hotter summer. As temperature records were smashed across Europe and other parts of the world, portable electric fans could be seen in the hands of millions of people. Estimates claim that up to 8 million of these devices were sold in the UK alone. The breeze that they provide will have been welcome to many, but could there be a downside to this popular product?

2  Concerns have been raised that these fans are just another example of fast technology. That is products that are sold cheaply and are likely to be disposed of quickly. Research from Material Focus, a British pro-recycling organisation, suggests that half of all the mini fans bought will end up unused or thrown away. This is unsurprising as they can be cheap to buy and almost impossible to repair. Fans contain a mix of different materials – plastic casing, copper wiring and a lithium-ion battery among other components. This means that a considerable amount of natural resource is used in their production, and that they can be complex to recycle and dispose of sustainably.

3  There are more immediate safety risks from portable fans. The London Fire Brigade has reported cases of cheaply-made portable fan batteries catching fire or exploding while being charged. Waste disposal companies in the UK have warned that the lithium-ion batteries used by these devices are often thrown away together with household waste, and that this can lead to fires which put staff and installations at risk. It's not just fire either. The Japanese Consumer Affairs Agency reports a train passenger's hair being sucked into someone else's fan on a train. In addition, once the air around you gets hot enough, fans can even make you warmer rather than colder.

4  As the world's climate continues to heat up, more and more of us may be tempted to reach for portable fans. But maybe we should take some time to reflect on the effect this might be having on our environment and climate.

item.title: The peacock effect: Why overconfidence can be good for you 孔雀效应：为什么过度自信可能对你有好处
item.description:
大多数人都更容易高估自己的聪明才智与经验技巧。如果自身能力不足以匹配这种认知，往往会引发严重的后果。但对于某些人来说，过度自信是否也能带来一些好处呢？阅读本文，了解 “overconfidence（过度自信）” 背后的心理学原理，以及为何研究人员会将其与孔雀的华丽羽毛联系在一起。

词汇：confidence 自信

1 Do you know anyone who is more confident in their own abilities than their actual performance suggests they should be? Perhaps they think they are an incredible singer, but they're actually tone-deaf. Most people believe that they are more intelligent and skilful than the average person, according to a 2020 meta-analysis by Zell and colleagues. Obviously, this cannot be the case. Overconfidence has a cost – it can lead to things like poor financial decisions and dangerous driving. So why do we have such a tendency to overestimate our abilities?

2 Excessive self-belief requires self-deception – believing your own falsehoods. An evolutionary perspective argues that humans evolved self-deception so that we could deceive others more easily. The theory goes that if you believe your own lies about your abilities, you're less likely to display behaviours which will give it away, such as nervousness or hesitation. Deceiving others about your abilities may enable you to open doors, but it is when you have to prove yourself that overconfidence can lead to costly mistakes. For those who have a greater underlying ability, though, overconfidence can be highly beneficial.

3 This is what researchers are calling the 'peacock's tail for people'. Peacocks have long and brightly coloured feathers to attract females, but they are extremely burdensome. The feathers are heavy and highly visible to predators, so only the healthiest peacocks can afford to carry such elaborate plumage. In other words, their feathers are a reliable indicator of their suitability for potential mates. Authors of a 2026 study, published in the Psychological Review compare this phenomenon with human overconfidence. They argue that only the most capable people can keep a high self-belief without suffering severe consequences. In other words, overconfidence may actually be a useful signal of ability.

4 So, what lessons can be learnt from all this? If you have a high ability in a particular skill, make sure you have the confidence to match it. Ability can bring success, but remember, it is confidence which opens the doors in the first place.

Confidence may make it easier to 3) _______ people about your abilities, but once you've opened the doors, you then have to 4) _______, and if your abilities don't match up, negative consequences can follow. But success can come when high 5) _______ is balanced with a high level of ability.

self-belief

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

答案

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 e) The costs of overconfidence
Paragraph 2 c) Overconfidence is part of human evolution
Paragraph 3 b) Confident humans are like healthy peacocks
Paragraph 4 a) The advice

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. a. True. Most people believe that they are more intelligent and skilful than the average person, according to a 2020 meta-analysis by Zell and colleagues.

2. b. False. Overconfidence has a cost – it can lead to things like poor financial decisions and dangerous driving. 

3. a. An evolutionary perspective argues that humans evolved self-deception so that we could deceive others more easily.

4. c. Authors of a 2026 study, published in the Psychological Review compare this phenomenon [the display of peacock feathers] with human overconfidence.

5. a. While overconfidence can be costly, it is largely positive due to its ability to open doors for people and be a useful signal of ability for those observing. 

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Humans have a tendency to be overconfident, believing their performance is better than it actually is. Confidence may make it easier to deceive people about your abilities, but once you've opened the doors, you then have to prove yourself, and if your abilities don't match up, negative consequences can follow. But success can come when high self-belief is balanced with a high level of ability.

item.title: Why don't I like rollercoasters anymore? 为什么我不再喜欢坐过山车了?
item.description:
小时候，过山车带来的惊险和刺激总让人乐此不疲。但随着年龄增长，身体的变化和对风险认知的提高，可能会让乘坐过山车变得不再那么轻松愉快。为什么人们在童年时期往往更能享受坐过山车的乐趣呢？阅读本文，了解其背后的科学原理，以及如何在长大后依然享受过山车带来的刺激。

词汇：thrill-seeking 寻求刺激

1 Rollercoasters have been making stomachs flip for centuries. The earliest versions appeared in 17th-century Russia, where brave riders slid down giant ice-covered ramps. Modern steel rollercoasters transformed theme parks into thrill-seeking playgrounds. Today, they're bigger, faster and taller than ever. Millions of people queue for hours just to experience a few minutes of screaming, laughing and that heart-racing drop. But if you're anything like me, there comes a point when those rides stop feeling exciting and start feeling... slightly regrettable.

2 As children, rollercoasters seem almost impossible to resist. Part of the appeal is that contrasting mix of fear and excitement. According to BBC Science Focus, rollercoasters trigger the body's fight-or-flight response, releasing adrenaline, dopamine and endorphins that make the experience feel exciting and rewarding. Our brains quickly learn to associate that rush with fun, which is why so many children can't wait to jump back in the queue. The sense of achievement doesn't hurt either – finally being tall enough to ride the biggest coaster feels like a rite of passage, making us feel braver and probably way cooler at the time.

3 So why does that love affair often fade with age? Unfortunately, our bodies change. WanderWisdom explains that changes in the inner ear as we get older can make us more sensitive to motion, meaning rollercoasters that once felt thrilling may now leave us feeling dizzy or nauseous. Motion sickness happens when the brain receives conflicting signals from the eyes and inner ear, leading to dizziness, nausea and that feeling of churning in your tummy. Add stiffer joints, sore necks and a stronger awareness of risk, and it's hardly surprising that the rides we once begged to go on can suddenly feel more exhausting than exhilarating.

4 The good news is that you don't have to completely give up coasters. Dramamine recommends staying hydrated, avoiding heavy meals before riding and looking towards the horizon instead of down at the tracks. Choosing a seat towards the middle can also make the ride feel less intense. These simple changes may reduce motion sickness and help you to rediscover the fun of laughing and screaming along the way without feeling the need to hurl or pass out as often!

测验与练习

一、为本文选择总结句。

a. Everyone loves rollercoasters when they're a kid.
b. It's impossible for you to get over your dislike of rollercoasters.
c. There are some things you can do to help make rollercoasters feel enjoyable.

二、 根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. The first rollercoasters were built from steel.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

2. According to the text, why do many children enjoy rollercoasters so much?
a. Their brains associate the rush of adrenaline with fun.
b. They are less likely to feel motion sickness than adults.
c. They enjoy waiting in long queues.

3. As people get older, changes to the inner ear can make rollercoasters feel more uncomfortable.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

4. Which of the following is NOT suggested as a way to reduce motion sickness?
a. Close your eyes throughout the ride.
b. Sit towards the middle of the ride.
c. Stay hydrated.

5. The writer says that adults should stop riding rollercoasters completely.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Have you ever felt like you might 1) _______ while riding a rollercoaster as an adult? Though you might experience a slight 2) _______, you're more likely as an adult to find rollercoasters 3) _______. This could be because of how 4) _______ our bodies become as we age, or that the changes in our ears make us feel 5) _______ from the motion of the ride.

beg
contrasting
dizzy
pass out
regrttable
rush
stiff

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

flip 翻腾
slide 滑行
thrill-seeking 追求刺激的
queue 排队
regrettable 令人后悔的
resist 抵挡，抗拒
contrasting 截然不同的，形成对比的
trigger 引发，触发
endorphin 内啡肽
rush 强烈的刺激感，兴奋感
rite of passage 成长的必经阶段
dizzy 头晕目眩的
conflicting 相互矛盾的
churning （胃里）翻腾的，反胃的
stiffer 更僵硬的
beg 恳求
exhilarating 令人兴奋的，令人振奋的
horizon 地平线
intense 剧烈的，强烈的
rediscover 重新找回，重新发现
hurl 呕吐
pass out 失去知觉，昏倒 

答案

一、 为本文选择总结句。

c. There are some things you can do to help make rollercoasters feel enjoyable

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. b. False. The earliest versions appeared in 17th-century Russia, where brave riders slid down giant ice-covered ramps.

2. a. Our brains quickly learn to associate that rush with fun, which is why so many children can't wait to jump straight back in the queue.

3. a. True. Changes to the inner ear as we get older can make us more sensitive to motion, meaning rollercoasters that once felt thrilling may now leave us feeling dizzy or nauseous

4. a. The text recommends staying hydrated, avoiding heavy meals before riding and looking towards the horizon instead of down at the tracks. Choosing a seat towards the middle can also make the ride feel less intense. It does not recommend closing your eyes.

5. b. False. The good news is that you don't have to completely give up coasters.

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Have you ever felt like you might pass out while riding a roller coaster as an adult? Though you might experience a slight rush, you’re more likely as an adult to find rollercoasters regrettable. This could be because of how stiff our bodies become as we age, or that the changes in our ears make us feel dizzy from the motion of the ride.

item.title: How seasons affect our moods 四季如何影响我们的情绪
item.description:
“春困秋乏夏打盹”，这句汉语俗语的背后是季节与人类情绪状态之间复杂的联系。从阳光明媚的春天到阴郁的冬日，我们的情绪和激素水平不断波动，塑造着我们对季节的独特印象。此外，每个人对四季的身体反应也不大相同。阅读本文，了解四季的更替究竟在如何调节我们的身体和情绪。

词汇：seasons 四季

1 We have four seasons in the UK. I like to think that spring gets its name from the flowers springing up to bloom. Next is my personal favourite – summer. I love the long, balmy evenings. Autumn, as some call fall, comes after. It's characterised by the orange and red leaves. Winter rolls around, and most of the vegetation is either decomposing or already dead, and the days are short and gloomy.

2 It's no wonder that, according to the Royal College of Psychiatrists, about three in every hundred people in the UK experience seasonal affective disorder, otherwise known as SAD. However, researchers at the Royal College of Psychiatrists have discovered that all seasons have an impact on our psychological functioning. It's also been found that hormones play an important role in seasonal mood changes as they fluctuate throughout the year.

3 An article published on Springer Nature Link observes positive emotional and physical changes to volunteers who were exposed to UVA from the Sun. Serotonin, known as 'the happy hormone', and dopamine, which is linked to motivation and pleasure, increases in months where there is a boost of sunlight. Similarly, lovers of spring recalibrate their energy and mood. After the cold, dark seasons of autumn and winter, it can feel like a biological reset.

4 Speaking of cold and dark, this is when those with naturally higher serotonin levels feel their mood regulating. They no longer feel overwhelmed by the high-level serotonin seasons of spring and summer. Reduced sunlight triggers higher melatonin, the sleepy hormone. There is the notion of preparing to slow down and get cosy, like that of animals in hibernation. It also rains more in autumn and winter. The Mind Company says that rain sounds reduce cortisol, the stress hormone, and helps you relax, focus and even sleep better.

5 We might like one season more than others. Our experience of seasons differs depending on location and environment. But one thing is for sure – our feelings change from season to season, and recognising these changes can help us act in ways that are in-line with our mental, emotional and physical capabilities.

测验与练习

一、为本文选择总结句。

a. How we feel doesn't change season to season.
b. How we feel may change depending on the season.
c. How we feel will determine the weather.

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. Which season in the UK sees leaves on the trees change from green to orange?
a. autumn
b. winter
c. spring

2. Our hormones change throughout the year.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

3. Sunny weather may increase _______ levels.
a. cortisol
b. dopamine
c. melatonin

4. People may prefer autumn and winter because…
a. there is less rainfall than spring and summer.
b. there is more sunlight than in spring and summer.
c. they feel overwhelmed by spring and summer.

5. The writer understands that people experience seasons differently.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

When we welcome a new season, our hormones 1) _______. This 2) _______ some changes in how we feel and behave. Some of us feel like we need a 3) _______ in sunlight to be happy. Others find peace in 4) _______ nights spent inside by a fireplace. Regardless of which season you prefer, it’s good to check in with yourself. This will help 5) _______ your emotions and direct your actions towards positivity.

balmy
boost
cosy
fluctuate
recalibrates
regulate
triggers

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

spring up 冒出来
bloom 绽放
balmy 温暖舒适的
roll around 再次到来
decompose 腐烂，分解
gloomy 阴郁的
disorder 疾病，紊乱
functioning 功能，运作
fluctuate 波动，起伏不定
UVA 长波紫外线
boost 增多，增强
recalibrate 重新调整
reset 重置
regulate 调节，稳定
overwhelm 使...不知所措，令...难以承受
trigger 导致，引起
notion 概念
cosy 舒适的，惬意的
hibernation 冬眠
in-line with 与…相似，与…处于同等水平

答案

一、为本文选择总结句。

b. How we feel may change depending on the season.

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. a. Autumn, as some call fall, comes after. It's characterised by the orange and red leaves.

2. a. True. It's also been found that hormones play an important role in seasonal mood changes as they fluctuate throughout the year.

3. b. Serotonin, known as the happy hormone, and dopamine, which is linked to motivation and pleasure, increases in months where there is a boost of sunlight.

4. c. Speaking of cold and dark, this is when those with naturally higher serotonin levels feel their mood regulating. They no longer feel overwhelmed by the high-level serotonin seasons of spring and summer.

5. a. True. We might like one season more than others. Our experience of seasons differs depending on location and environment.

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

When we welcome a new season, our hormones fluctuate. This triggers some changes in how we feel and behave. Some of us feel like we need a boost in sunlight to be happy. Others find peace in cosy nights spent inside by a fireplace. Regardless of which season you prefer, it’s good to check in with yourself. This will help regulate your emotions and direct your actions more positively.
